promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: You ran a very big week and felt great, which is a nice sign, but the jump from 37 to 53 miles was too much too fast. Next week pulls back a touch, adds marathon-pace work, and protects the long run arc into the race.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer: Short answer: no, please do not keep stacking miles like that. You felt fine because you are fit and motivated, but a 43 percent jump in one week is exactly how healthy runners pick up a tendon or hip niggle, and you had a knee flare only a month ago on a far smaller build. The gain from this week has to be absorbed before it becomes fitness, so next week steps back to about 43 miles with real marathon-pace work. From here the long run grows once more to around 20 miles with marathon-pace segments, then we taper. If a session feels easy, hold the extra for the race.

new.analysis:
The week you ran was a strong one, just too strong for where you are in the build. Every day drifted longer than planned, and the long run jumped from a planned 15 to 20 miles with the club. Six-week marathon builds succeed by banking the next long run and the next quality session, not by chasing a single big week.

The long run itself tells the story. Pace was steady at 10:02, but heart rate climbed from 145 to 153 and the run spent 88 percent in zone 3, which means it cost more than it looked on the watch. Soreness in the calves on Sunday night fits that picture. We absorb that this week with a slightly lower total and keep the quality specific to the race.

Next week introduces marathon pace, around 8:30 per mile for a sub-3:45. Wednesday is a controlled dose inside a shorter tempo, and the long run finishes with four miles at goal pace so the legs learn what it feels like on tired legs. Easy days stay honest at heart rate under 145, Tuesday and Thursday both, because that is where the aerobic base is actually built.

From here the shape is: one more big long run at five weeks out with more marathon-pace work, a peak long run at four weeks out, then three weeks of taper. The fitness is already there for your goal if we land the race healthy, so the job for the next three weeks is restraint, not heroics.

safetyCallouts.title: Calves tight Sunday night.
safetyCallouts.body: If tightness lingers through Tuesday or turns into sharp pain, back off and see a physio rather than running through it.
